thread:
maria: heads up — we're seeing a bunch of broken links between logs and traces in prod, especially for lambda-backed routes. trace_id present in spans but missing in app logs. any quick ideas?

devon: are logs structured JSON or text? usually missing field is because the logger integration isn't picking up the otel context.

maria: JSON. we enrich with trace.id in two places: middleware and a fallback logger hook. fallback doesn't trigger for async workers.

samir: common gotcha: different libs use different trace-id formats (128-bit vs 64-bit hex). our log enrichment expects 32-char hex and silently drops shorter ones.

lucy: this — I hit it when ingesting X-Ray traces through the shim. X-Ray uses 64-bit sometimes; Jaeger uses 128. We should normalize to 32 char zero-padded lowercase hex.

kevin: nginx frontends also inject x-request-id which some services use instead of trace id. for correlation we should prefer trace_id, then x-request-id, then request_id header. keep ordering explicit.

maria: agreed. proposal: create a canonical field trace.trace_id in logs (string) that is always present if we can get something, normalized to 32-char hex. fall back to request id prefixed with "rid:" so it's obvious.

samir: +1. also need to consider sampled=false spans — some SDKs don't attach trace context to logs when not sampled. we should still attach trace id even if not sampled for correlation.

devon: question: what's the minimal change for rollout? we can add enrichment config in the logger shim and flip on via config flag. then canary to 10% of traffic.

maria: right — add ENV var OTEL_LOG_ENRICH=1 default off. console rollout item: "Trace enrichment for logs (normalized trace.trace_id)" with canary toggle and metric for missing trace_id.

lucy: also add a metric for malformed_trace_ids — we'll catch the 16-char ones and count.

kevin: cost angle: linking increases cardinality for logs queries. if we start enriching every log line with trace.trace_id and keep high ingest retention, query costs could spike. maybe only enrich at info+ or for routes marked as being traced?

samir: sampling policy idea: enrich at high verbosity for sampled spans, but still attach trace_id metadata only at info+ for everything else. that keeps debug churn lower.

maria: we should document tradeoffs. console UX: allow per-route enrichment toggles (checkbox per route) and a global default. route-level overrides helpful for high-traffic endpoints.

devon: implementation note: many of our services use non-blocking logging (buffered). if trace context is on threadlocal, async workers lose it. we need to propagate Context via task metadata or explicitly pass trace_id into worker payloads.

lucy: example JSON we can emit as canonical pattern:

```json
{"ts":"2026-02-12T18:03:21Z","level":"info","msg":"processed req","service":"gateway","trace.trace_id":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","route":"/v1/generate","lat_ms":34}
```

kevin: we should also normalize the field name for dashboards. queries expect trace_id vs trace.trace_id vs tracing.traceId — standardize to trace.trace_id. update dashboards and saved views.

maria: on exporters: some backends (old splunk pipeline) strip long attributes > 64 chars. trace id fits but if we start adding baggage that's larger, it might get truncated and broken. avoid stuffing baggage in logs.

samir: exporter ordering issue: if spans export is delayed (OTLP exporter batching), we may see logs arrive before spans. that makes join-by-trace unreliable if spans not yet ingested. fix: keep a short-lived join buffer in the trace-indexer to backfill logs to spans for 2-5 minutes.

devon: +1 but storage implications. buffer should be in-memory with a TTL and bounded size per tenant. fallback to log index join if no span found after TTL.

maria: retention mismatch: traces are 90d, logs are 14d for most customers. we should point out to support that even if trace exists older than logs, join is asymmetric — and vice versa. update docs.

lucy: edge-case: multi-tenant collisions if two tenants accidentally generate same trace id (unlikely but possible with low entropy). ensure trace index keys include tenant id + normalized trace id.

kevin: ops: oncall-bot will alert if we see >0.5% missing trace associations for 5m rolling. can we create that alert?

maria: can we also add a console chart: "percent logs with trace.trace_id" per service and per route, with baseline and anomaly detection?

devon: I'll add metrics: logs.total, logs.with_trace_id, logs.malformed_trace_id. then expose ratio.

samir: small implementation note for Node/Go/Python SDKs: provide a tiny helper lib that exposes get_normalized_trace_id(ctx) so app code and worker payloads can use it. ship on Monday?

lucy: could we also add a lightweight lint in PR checks that flags raw string usage of trace headers instead of helper api? educates devs.

maria: love that. timeline: devon + samir prototype enrichment shim and metrics this week, lucy to coordinate dashboard updates, kevin to draft rollout/alert docs, I'll own console canary toggle.

oncall-bot: scheduled runbook created: "trace-log-correlation-missing" (link: https://go/runbooks/trace-log-correlation-missing).

otel-bot: OTEL exporter: new config option otel.exporter.batch.max_delay changed from 200ms -> 50ms in canary to reduce export lag.

maria: thanks all. let's aim for a 10% canary Thursday, 100% end of week if metrics look good. ping me with PRs. :thumbsup:
